s1.syndrome_frame: A tender, palpable mass in the buttock or perineum with recent onset of constipation and numbness of the lower extremity
salient_findings: Tender, palpable mass in the left buttock
Numbness of the left lower extremity worsened by sitting
Hypoesthesia in the L5-S4 distribution on the left
key_facts: 21-year-old man with no past medical or surgical history
Tender, palpable mass in the left buttock noticed for several years
Mass rapidly enlarged over the previous six months
Recent onset of constipation
Numbness of the left lower extremity worsened by sitting
No drainage, redness, fever, or systemic symptoms
No medications or family history of cancer
4 × 4 cm tender mass palpated in the left perineum
Hypoesthesia in the L5-S4 distribution on the left with intact motor function
Abdominal and digital rectal examinations were unremarkable
Contrast-enhanced CT of the pelvis revealed a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion
Contrast-enhanced MRI showed homogeneous, T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense lesions with no wall enhancement

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a cystic lesion in the perineum with nerve compression symptoms

shortlist.label: Pilonidal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a tender, palpable mass in the buttock or perineum

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a cystic lesion in the perineum, although less likely than Tarlov cyst

shortlist.label: Perineal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Although the patient has no signs of infection, an abscess cannot be entirely ruled out

shortlist.label: Pudendal nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that could cause nerve compression symptoms and a palpable mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion on CT and homogeneous, T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense lesions with no wall enhancement on MRI, along with the location near the pudendal canal and symptoms such as numbness in the L5-S4 distribution, are consistent with a Tarlov cyst.

rejected.label: Pilonidal cyst
rejected.why: Typically presents with drainage, redness, and fever, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Usually has a thicker wall and may show enhancement on imaging, not consistent with the homogeneous, nonenhancing appearance on CT and MRI

rejected.label: Perineal abscess
rejected.why: Would likely present with signs of infection such as fever, redness, and drainage, which are absent in this case

rejected.label: Pudendal nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: Would more likely show enhancement on imaging due to its solid nature and may not present as a purely cystic lesion
